scenario: AITA for Refusing to Pump my GF's Tire? | Whenever my GF's car has any sort of maintenance issue she tries to hold me accountable for finding the issue, fixing it, or taking it to get fixed. When she had an issue with one of her tires a while ago I was the first to notice how low it was and gave her a heads up as she was leaving for work. A day later it was completely flat because she didn't pump air in it (or get it inspected). So I ended up doing it for her. At that time I also decided to buy her PSI gauge and showed her how to use it. This was about the extent of my capabilities and when I started to notice a pattern of other car-related demands I made it very clear that I don't know shit about fixing cars besides the very basics (changing a tire, pumping air, pouring oil, jumps starts). She still insisted that I call her Dad and ask questions or watch youtube videos to learn how. My response was that I'd prefer that a mechanic take care of it and that she could learn to do these things if she wanted. ​ Now another tire has a slow leak and needs to be refilled about once a week or two (not entirely sure bc I've never seen it completely flat). She insists that I check the pressure every morning before work and drive it to the gas station to fill the tire as needed (until she gets it fixed/replaced). She says she never noticed the leak before and had to rely on the help of strangers to check the pressure and pump the tire for her. ​ I asked why she needed strangers (they're always men btw) to do something that I've taught her how to do already. She claimed that she didn't know how, didn't want to get dirty, and ultimately its a man's responsibility. I told her that as a car owner (man or woman) you should know how do something as basic as pump a tire and change a flat (especially since I showed her how). I told her that it seemed like she was playing the "Damsel in distress" role and acting completely helpless on purpose. I also reminded her that she could be stranded one day and may need to know how to do these things instead of relying on the generosity of complete strangers. She replied saying that all of her male friends/family agreed with her and that they were "real men" b/c they knew how to take care of a woman. ​ I don't really care for the silly, outdated gender role bs and I've made it very clear. On top of that I do plenty of handy work around the house, cook and clean regularly ( I cook more often than she does in fact), and I pay majority of our expenses (including all of the rent). The way I see it, this shouldn't make me any less of a man in her eyes. I also never hold her to lofty standards, or stereotypical expectations just bc she's a woman, but she always seems comfortable doing it to me. ​ To settle the issue, I offered again to show her how to use the pump while we were at the gas station this past weekend. She flatly refused..... So now I'm determined not to lift a finger. AITA here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (A Guy In Trouble) in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario. My girlfriend has a car that's been having maintenance issues, and she tends to hold me accountable for fixing them or getting them fixed. The first time, she had a tire issue, and I noticed it was low. I told her, and a day later, it was flat because she didn't pump air into it or get it inspected. I ended up fixing it for her and even bought her a PSI gauge to show her how to use it. But I made it clear that I don't know much about fixing cars beyond basics like changing a tire, pumping air, pouring oil, and jump starts. Now, another tire has a slow leak and needs to be refilled about once a week or two. She insists that I check the pressure every morning before work and drive to the gas station to fill it as needed until she gets it fixed or replaced. She claims she didn't notice the leak before and had to rely on strangers to check the pressure and pump the tire for her. I asked why she needed strangers (who are always men) to do something I've already taught her how to do. She said she didn't know how, didn't want to get dirty, and that it's a man's responsibility. I told her that as a car owner, whether man or woman, she should know how to do something as basic as pumping a tire and changing a flat, especially since I showed her how. I mentioned that it seemed like she was playing the "Damsel in Distress" role and acting completely helpless on purpose. I reminded her that she could be stranded one day and need to know how to do these things instead of relying on strangers. She replied that all her male friends and family agreed with her and that they were "real men" because they knew how to take care of a woman. I don't care for these outdated gender roles and have made it clear. Plus, I do plenty of handywork around the house, cook and clean regularly (I cook more than she does), and pay the majority of our expenses, including her rent. I don't hold her to lofty standards or stereotypical expectations just because she's a woman, but she seems comfortable doing that to me. To settle the issue, I offered again to show her how to use the pump while we were at the gas station this past weekend, but she flatly refused. Now I'm determined not to lift a finger. Am I AITA here? Hmm, so I need to figure out if I'm being unreasonable or if my girlfriend is. Let me break it down. First, I took the initiative to fix her tire when it went flat, even though she didn't take care of it. I also bought her a gauge and taught her how to use it. But I made it clear that I don't know much about cars beyond the basics. She still insists I handle other car-related issues, even though I've shown her how to do some things. Now, with the slow leak, she wants me to check the pressure every morning and drive to the gas station to pump it. She claims she didn't know how and didn't want to get dirty, and she thinks it's a man's responsibility. I told her she should know how to do it, as it's a basic skill for a car owner, and I showed her how. I also pointed out that relying on strangers isn't reliable and could leave her stranded. She countered by saying her male friends and family agree with her and that they're "real men" because they take care of women. I don't buy into these outdated gender roles and have been handling a lot of the household responsibilities, including paying most of the expenses. I don't hold her to traditional expectations, but she seems to hold me to them. I offered to teach her again, but she refused. Now I'm not going to help anymore. Is that AITA? I think AITA is when a guy is being unreasonable or unfair in a situation, often due to gendered expectations. In this case, I'm trying to empower her to take care of her own car, which is a responsible thing. I've already taught her how to pump a tire and gave her a gauge. She's choosing not to learn or do it herself, instead relying on me or strangers. She's also using gender roles to justify her behavior, which I find outdated and unfair. I'm handling more than my share of responsibilities, and she's not contributing in this area. I'm not asking her to do everything, but I think it's reasonable to expect her to handle basic car maintenance, especially since I've shown her how. By refusing to help anymore, I'm setting a boundary. It's not fair for me to always be the one responsible for her car issues when she has the capability to handle it. I'm not being mean; I'm encouraging her to be self-sufficient, which is a good life skill. So, in this case, I don't think I'm AITA. I'm being reasonable by expecting her to take responsibility for her own car, especially since I've already provided the tools and knowledge. She's the one clinging to outdated gender roles and refusing to take initiative, which is putting the burden on me unnecessarily.
